target_experiment: In acute APAP mice (600 mg/kg), anti-MIF preserved hepatic dendritic cells and reduced injury. In acute CCl4, CD74 siRNA in mouse hepatocytes reduced MIF-induced MCP-1.
counter_evidence: In metabolic liver injury models MIF-CD74/AMPK protected hepatocytes from lipid accumulation. Acute anti-MIF benefit leaves the effect of direct CD74 blockade during APAP recovery unresolved.
compound_action: Binds human CD74; annotated antagonist. Functional blockade of hepatic MIF-CD74 signaling is unknown.
activity_type: Human anti-CD74 antibody in phase I lymphoma study
liver_evidence: Direct antibody evidence in APAP injury or recovery is unknown. Anti-MIF experiments perturbed the ligand.
selectivity: Native human CD74 binder; mouse CD74 engagement and functional selectivity in liver are unknown.
liabilities: Infusion reactions and apparent binding outside the tumor in previously treated lymphoma patients.
decision: Unresolved. Antibody comparator only. A suitable direct small-molecule candidate with APAP evidence was not established; repotrectinib targets the CD74–ROS1 fusion.

target_experiment: Whole-body Gal-3 loss in APAP-treated mice (300 mg/kg) reduced hepatotoxicity most strongly at 48–72 h; Gal-3 was found in mononuclear cells in necrotic areas. A companion study found altered macrophage composition and more hepatocyte mitoses during recovery.
counter_evidence: TD139 raised serum ALT in HBs-Tg mice and increased hepatic conventional NK cell activation. This is a different disease and immune context. Genetic loss in APAP also differs from post-injury drug dosing.
compound_action: Competes for the galectin carbohydrate-recognition domain.
activity_type: Kd, isothermal titration calorimetry with purified human Gal-3 carbohydrate-recognition domain
liver_evidence: Higher ALT in TD139-treated HBs-Tg mice; acute APAP pharmacology and recovery remain unknown in the reviewed studies.
selectivity: Also binds human Gal-1. Mouse Gal-3 affinity can differ from human Gal-3 affinity.
liabilities: Elevated ALT in HBs-Tg mice is a context-specific experimental signal; APAP safety is unknown.
decision: Unresolved. Mechanistic probe for the APAP hypothesis if exposure, mouse engagement, Gal-1 activity, and recovery can be measured.

target_experiment: Macrophage-derived CTSS generated endostatin and promoted hepatic stellate cell activation and fibrosis. CTSS inhibition reduced fibrosis markers and serum ALT in mice after chronic CCl4.
counter_evidence: Chronic matrix remodeling and acute APAP repair have different time scales and endpoints. Direct evidence resolving CTSS effects on acute APAP injury versus repair was not identified in this review.
activity_type: IC50, fluorogenic inhibition assay with purified human CTSS
liver_evidence: 5 mg/kg i.p. every two days for two weeks after ten weeks of CCl4 in mice reduced collagen, stellate cell activation, endostatin and ALT. Acute APAP outcomes are unknown.
selectivity: Discovery study reports selectivity across tested cathepsins; broader off-target activity in injured liver is unknown.
liabilities: After single oral doses in healthy volunteers, plasma CTSS activity initially fell and subsequently rebounded above baseline.
decision: Follow-up candidate for chronic fibrosis only. Acute APAP intervention remains unresolved.
